Aisha.evidence: Feminine active participle of عَاشَ, “to live”; given name Aisha.

Abeer.evidence: عَبِير: scent, perfume; female given name Abeer.

Abhinav.evidence: अभिनव: new, young, modern, fresh; given name Abhinav.

Abhishek.evidence: अभिषेक: anointing, inaugurating or consecrating; given name Abhishek.

Abheesht.evidence: अभीष्ट: desired, wished, cherished, beloved; names Abhisht and Abheesht.

Abhisht.evidence: अभीष्ट: desired, wished, cherished, beloved; names Abhisht and Abheesht.

Adithya.meaning: A Sanskrit name associated with the sun and the children of the goddess Aditi.
Adithya.evidence: आदित्य: sons of Aditi; a name of Surya; the sun.

Aditya.meaning: A Sanskrit name associated with the sun and the children of the goddess Aditi.
Aditya.evidence: आदित्य: sons of Aditi; a name of Surya; the sun.

Aishwarya.meaning: From a Sanskrit root meaning “power” or “sovereignty”.

Ajay.evidence: अजय: unconquerable, invincible, victorious; given name Ajay.

Akash.evidence: आकाश: sky, space, cosmos; given name Akash.

Akhil.evidence: अखिल: complete, whole; given name Akhil.

Akshat.evidence: अक्षत: uninjured, unbroken, whole; given name Akshat.

Amala.meaning: From a Sanskrit root meaning “spotless”, “clean” or “pure”.
Amala.evidence: अमला is from अमल, spotless, stainless, clean, pure, shining.

Ambar.meaning: From a Sanskrit word for “sky” or “atmosphere”.

Anant.evidence: अनन्त: endless, boundless, eternal, infinite; given name Anant.

Ananta.evidence: अनन्त: endless, boundless, eternal, infinite; given name Anant.

Ananya.evidence: अनन्य: matchless, unique, without equal; given name Ananya.

Ahmed.evidence: أحمد: elative of حميد; more or most praiseworthy; given name Ahmed.

Adel.meaning: An Arabic form of Adil, linked to “just” or “fair”.

Afeefa.meaning: From an Arabic root meaning “chaste”, “pure” or “virtuous”.

Hamid.evidence: حميد: praiseworthy; male given name Hamid.

Amin.evidence: أمين: reliable, trustworthy, faithful, honest; male given name Amin.

Amina.meaning: From an Arabic name linked to “safe” or “secure”.
Amina.evidence: آمِن: safe, secure; آمِنَة is its feminine and a given name.

Halima.meaning: From an Arabic name linked to “patient” or “forbearing”.
Halima.evidence: حليم: patient, forbearing; حليمة is its feminine and a given name.

Khaled.evidence: خالد: immortal, eternal; male given names Khalid and Khaled.

Jamil.evidence: جميل: beautiful, handsome; male given name Jamil.

Latif.meaning: From an Arabic root meaning “gentle”, “kind” or “graceful”.
Latif.evidence: لطيف: gentle, kind, graceful; لطيفة is its feminine.

Latifa.meaning: From an Arabic root meaning “gentle”, “kind” or “graceful”.
Latifa.evidence: لطيف: gentle, kind, graceful; لطيفة is its feminine.

Imane.evidence: إيمان: belief, faith; female given name.

Mansour.evidence: منصور: triumphant, victorious; given names Mansur and Mansour.

Mansur.evidence: منصور: triumphant, victorious; given names Mansur and Mansour.

Murad.evidence: مُرَاد: wanted, wished for, desired; male given name Murad.

Loujain.evidence: لجين: refined silver; female given name.

Achraf.meaning: From Arabic for “most noble” or “most honoured”.
Achraf.evidence: أشرف: more or most noble and honored; male given name Ashraf.

Ashraf.meaning: From Arabic for “most noble” or “most honoured”.
Ashraf.evidence: أشرف: more or most noble and honored; male given name Ashraf.

Ayman.meaning: An Arabic name associated with “lucky” and “right-handed”.
Ayman.evidence: أيمن: lucky; right-handed; male given name.

Manal.evidence: منال: achievement, attainment, obtaining; given name Manal.

Jafar.evidence: جعفر: full river; brook, creek, rivulet; given name Jafar.

Jawad.evidence: جواد: generous, bountiful; male given name Jawad.

Basit.meaning: From an Arabic word meaning “wide”, “extended” or “simple”.
Basit.evidence: بسيط: wide, extended, spread out; easy, simple.

Caolan.meaning: From an Irish name built from “slender” or “narrow” and a diminutive ending.
Caolan.evidence: Caolán: caol, slender or narrow, plus -án.

Ciaran.meaning: From an Irish name built from “black” or “dark” and a diminutive ending.
Ciaran.evidence: Ciarán: Old Irish Cíarán, from ciar, black, plus -án.

Bronagh.meaning: From an Irish name meaning “sad” or “sorrowful”.
Bronagh.evidence: Brónach: brónach, sad, sorrowful; equivalent to English Bronagh.

Hywel.meaning: From a Welsh name meaning “eminent” or “conspicuous”.
Hywel.evidence: Hywel: male given name meaning eminent or conspicuous.

Howel.meaning: From a Welsh name meaning “eminent” or “conspicuous”.
Howel.evidence: Hywel: male given name meaning eminent or conspicuous.

Howell.meaning: From a Welsh name meaning “eminent” or “conspicuous”.
Howell.evidence: Hywel: male given name meaning eminent or conspicuous.

Cathal.meaning: From an Irish name traced to a Celtic root meaning “strong in battle”.
Cathal.evidence: Cathal from Proto-Celtic *Katuwalos, strong in battle.

Carwyn.evidence: Carwyn: caru, love, plus gwyn, blessed.

Connel.meaning: From an Irish name built from Celtic roots for “hound” and “prince” or “chief”.
Connel.evidence: Conall: *kū, dog or hound, plus *walos, prince or chief.

Fenella.meaning: From an Irish name built from “fair” and “shoulder”.
Fenella.evidence: Fionnghuala: find, fair, plus guala, shoulder; equivalent to English Fenella.

Bridget.meaning: From an Irish name traced to a Celtic root meaning “high” or “exalted”.
Bridget.evidence: Bríd from *Brigantī, high, exalted; English equivalents Bridget and Brigid.

Brigid.meaning: From an Irish name traced to a Celtic root meaning “high” or “exalted”.
Brigid.evidence: Bríd from *Brigantī, high, exalted; English equivalents Bridget and Brigid.

Eitan.evidence: איתן: strong, firm, enduring, permanent; given name equivalent to Ethan.

Amatullah.evidence: أمة الله: أمة, slave, plus الله, God; literally servant of God.

Atef.evidence: عاطف: compassionate; male given name Atef.

Kaleem.meaning: From an Arabic word for “one who speaks with another person”.
Kaleem.evidence: كَلِيم: one who speaks with another person.

Mujib.meaning: From an Arabic root meaning “one who answers” or “responds”.
Mujib.evidence: مُجِيب: active participle of أجاب, to respond, reply, answer.

Masoud.evidence: مسعود: happy, lucky; male given name.

Adina.meaning: From a Hebrew root meaning “gentle” or “mild”.
Adina.evidence: עדינה from עדין, gentle or mild; female given name Adina.

Amit.evidence: עמית: colleague, friend, comrade; male given name Amit.

Merav.evidence: מרב: maximum; female given name Merav.

Jael.meaning: From Hebrew for “ibex”, a wild mountain goat.
Jael.evidence: יעל: ibex; female given name equivalent to Yael.

Acacius.meaning: From an Ancient Greek root meaning “harmless”.
Acacius.evidence: Ἀκάκιος from ἄκακος, harmless; given name Acacius.

Agathon.meaning: From an Ancient Greek root meaning “good”.
Agathon.evidence: Ἀγάθων from ἀγαθός, good; equivalent to English Agathon.

Agatharchus.meaning: From Ancient Greek roots for “good” and “ruler”.
Agatharchus.evidence: Ἀγάθαρχος from ἀγαθός, good, plus ἀρχός, ruler; given name Agatharchus.

Eugenius.meaning: From an Ancient Greek root meaning “well-born”.

Ariadne.meaning: Traditionally linked to Greek for “very holy” or “very pure”; a pre-Greek origin has also been proposed.
Ariadne.evidence: Classical scholars: ἀρι-, very, plus ἀδνός, holy or pure; Beekes proposes Pre-Greek origin.

Gwyn.evidence: Welsh gwyn: white, blessed; name Gwyn is a nominalised adjective.

Gwynn.evidence: Welsh gwyn: white, blessed; name Gwyn is a nominalised adjective.

Gwynne.evidence: Welsh gwyn: white, blessed; name Gwyn is a nominalised adjective.

Domhnall.meaning: From a Celtic name built from “world” and “prince” or “chief”.
Domhnall.evidence: *Dubnowalos from *dubnos, world, plus *walos, prince or chief.

Husayn.meaning: A diminutive of Hasan, an Arabic name linked to “good” or “handsome”.
Husayn.evidence: Husayn: diminutive of Hasan meaning good or handsome; Hocine borrows Arabic حسين.

Hocine.meaning: A diminutive of Hasan, an Arabic name linked to “good” or “handsome”.
Hocine.evidence: Husayn: diminutive of Hasan meaning good or handsome; Hocine borrows Arabic حسين.

Ieesha.meaning: A form of Aisha, an Arabic name meaning “living”.
Ieesha.evidence: Aisha is feminine active participle of عَاشَ, to live; Ieesha and Iesha are phonetic spellings.

Iesha.meaning: A form of Aisha, an Arabic name meaning “living”.
Iesha.evidence: Aisha is feminine active participle of عَاشَ, to live; Ieesha and Iesha are phonetic spellings.

Adit.meaning: A short form of Aditya, a Sanskrit name associated with the sun.
Adit.evidence: Aditya: the sun, name of Surya; Adit is a hypocorism of Aditya.

Abdulmalik.evidence: عبد: servant; مَلِك: king, sovereign, monarch.

Abdulrazzak.evidence: عبد: servant; رزاق: the Provider, of God.

Khadija.meaning: From an Arabic root meaning “early” or “premature”.
Khadija.evidence: خديج: premature, early; خديجة is its feminine and a female given name.
